# Contributing

Thanks for helping make this list more useful for people traveling to Korea.

## What we accept

- Official portals and primary sources (VisitKorea, Korea.net, Korail, K-ETA, city tourism sites).
- Free or freemium tools, apps, and booking platforms that genuinely help travelers.
- Guides and explainers that go past surface-level and link to primary sources.
- Multilingual resources (Korean, Vietnamese, Russian, Mandarin Chinese).

## What we don't accept

- Paid tours and gated content as the only link for a topic.
- Affiliate-stuffed listicles, ad-driven blogs, and sponsored placements.
- Outdated guides that have not been updated for current rules (K-ETA, visa-free terms, fares).
- Resources that duplicate one already on the list without adding something new.

## How to add a resource

1. Open a pull request that edits `README.md`.
2. Add one line in the format `- [Name](URL) - short, factual description of what it covers.`
3. Keep topical order within the section.
4. If your resource is in a language other than English, add the language code in brackets at the end: `[ko]`, `[vi]`, `[ru]`, `[zh]`.
5. In the PR description, say briefly why this resource is worth adding and how it helped a trip you or someone you know took.

## Style rules

- Plain language. One sentence per line item, factual not promotional.
- No em dashes. Use commas, colons, or a new sentence.
- Korean terms: English first, Korean in parentheses on first mention. Example: `Climate Card (기후동행카드)`.
- Romanize Korean place names (Seoul, Busan, Jeju, Gyeongju), not localized spellings.

## Reporting a broken or outdated link

Open an issue using the "Report broken or outdated resource" template. We try to triage these within a week.

## Code of Conduct

This project follows the [Contributor Covenant](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Be kind.
